What does corporate transportation in Scottsdale cover?

Four movements on one reservation: airport arrivals and departures for a visiting team, executive day programmes between offices and hotels, convention and event shuttles, and multi-day programmes. Every vehicle is booked by the hour, on a 4-hour minimum, or as a one-way transfer. The unit of sale is time, not distance or headcount: you buy a vehicle and a chauffeur for a block of hours. One airport run is the exception, priced as a trip: flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off — $295 one way in the Executive Black Sprinter, plus $50 a stop — and beyond that priced from the drive, with the empty return included and the basis on the quote. What it is not is event management. This company books vehicles and coordinates them — "Several vehicles on one booking, coordinated to one schedule with one point of contact" — while the venue and the agenda stay yours.

Which vehicles does a corporate booking put on the road?

The pool runs from 8 seats to 56 across the executive units: Executive Black Sprinter at $145 an hour at one end, 56-Passenger Motorcoach at $325 an hour at the other. Starting totals run $580 to $1,625 before 8% tax — about $29 a seat in the largest coach. Read the table as this route's own recommendation rather than a catalogue: it is the pool the vehicle picker, the "From" rate and this page's structured data all resolve through, and it carries proper seats only, never a celebration cabin. Starting total is the hourly rate times the billable hours at that vehicle's own minimum, before 8% Arizona tax. Bags are the cap the counter enforces, and rows with no owner-confirmed number say so. How do you handle airport arrivals for a whole team?

Two shapes. A group landing together is a transfer — $295 one way in the Executive Black Sprinter, $1,250 in the 56-Passenger Motorcoach, $50 for each added stop. A team arriving across a day is an hourly booking run in waves. On any airport leg: "Flight tracking on airport legs" So the flight number belongs on the reservation. A meet-and-greet is the one airport extra, arranged rather than included: "Optional airport greeter at baggage claim with a name sign and help with bags — $200 flat for airport transfers, confirmed with your quote." That $200 is the add-on catalogue's own price, chosen with the quote. Sky Harbor group arrivals have their own service page, and the Phoenix airport to Scottsdale guide covers the drive; both are linked below. No terminal, curb or drive time is stated here, because none of those is ours to publish.

How does a convention or event shuttle work?

As an hourly block against a written plan. One Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) moves 29 riders a circuit and the 56-Passenger Motorcoach moves 56; repeating that circuit costs no more than the hours already booked. What it is not is a timetable. The two shapes this company publishes are the whole basis of this section: "Arrival and departure runs split into waves across the vehicles" and "A written movement plan before the date — vehicle by vehicle, pickup by pickup" A wave suits arrival and departure days, when a group lands across a window: each run is a named departure with its own rider list, and the hourly block has already bought the time. A loop suits the middle of a programme, hotel to venue and back. Neither is a printed interval: "Where a vehicle of your size may stop, and how close that is to the door — the venue sets that on the night." For 20 to 29 riders read the executive minibus group shuttle; for the coach class, the charter bus rental guide.

What does the office need before it can quote?

Addresses, a headcount, times and one name. Every movement's exact street address goes on the booking, the rider count and whether it is firm, the arrival time you need, and one on-site contact. Cargo is listed separately: 125 bags is the top of the published range. Seats and cargo are two questions, and the second decides more bookings than planners expect: "Passenger capacity is a seating limit, not cargo space. List banner cases, pop-up displays, sample boxes and crew gear when you request the quote so the fit is confirmed in writing rather than discovered at the curb." Accessibility belongs in the same message: "Mobility and accessibility needs — a walker or wheelchair, a folding mobility scooter, a low step, a seat near the door, or a short walk from the drop point." And this is not ours to settle early: "Anything the venue or your own company requires of an arriving vehicle."

What does the corporate hourly rate include?

The vehicle, the chauffeur and the fuel, plus 8% Arizona tax and nothing else. A day of 7 hours or more earns free hours against the bill, and add-ons are chosen at checkout rather than assumed. 3 vehicles or fewer price themselves; more is quoted in writing. The published inclusion list applies to any chauffeured booking. "A professional chauffeur on every vehicle, background- and MVR-checked" "Tax only — no booking fee, no service charge, no fuel surcharge, and gratuity never added for you" One is easy to miss on a long corporate day: "Free hours as the day gets longer: 7–11 hours earns 1, 12–14 earns 2, 15 or more earns 3" Not included: anything added at checkout — a greeter, a child seat, extra hours — and what a property charges for access. Two house rules: "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop." and "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really."

Planning a company holiday party

A holiday party is three movements in one night: collecting people from the office or a hotel, arriving at the venue together, and getting everyone home at the end — which is later, and messier, than anyone plans for.

One reservation covers all three. Bring the answers below and the quote comes back in writing, with the vehicles named.

Bring these and we can quote it

  • Where the group starts: the office, one hotel, several hotels, or people making their own way to a single meeting point.
  • How many are riding, and whether that number is confirmed or still moving.
  • The venue address, and the arrival time you want people inside rather than the time you want to leave.
  • Whether guests bring coats, gifts, awards, décor or equipment, because those take seats or luggage room.
  • Mobility and accessibility needs — a walker or wheelchair, a folding mobility scooter, a low step, a seat near the door, or a short walk from the drop point.
  • How the night ends: everyone together at one time, or return waves as people leave.
  • One on-site contact we can reach, so the chauffeur works from a written schedule instead of a group chat.

Settled closer to the date

Not ours to promise weeks out, so we confirm them with you rather than print them here.

  • Where a vehicle of your size may stop, and how close that is to the door — the venue sets that on the night.
  • Exact late-hour return waves, which settle once the headcount and the end time are real.
  • Availability on your date, which is confirmed in writing before anything is reserved.
  • Anything the venue or your own company requires of an arriving vehicle.

Fit decides the vehicle: executive seating for the ride to dinner and the ride home, in Sprinters, mini buses and coaches up to the 56-seat 56-Passenger Motorcoach. If the party is meant to start in the vehicle, ask for a party cabin and the quote is written for that instead. Neither is assumed.

What is corporate transportation?

Corporate transportation is chauffeured ground transportation that a company books for its people and its guests: airport arrivals and departures, executive days between offices and hotels, conference and event shuttles, and team outings. In Scottsdale and Phoenix, Scottsdale Sprinters runs it in executive vehicles only, from the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter for 8 to the 56-Passenger Motorcoach for 56, each with a professional chauffeur.

Each vehicle is booked by the hour on its own minimum (7 or more hours earns 1 free hour, 12 or more hours earns 2 free hours, 15 or more hours earns 3 free hours) or as a one-way transfer, flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off; longer transfers are priced from the drive with the empty return included. Figures are before 8% Arizona sales tax. One reservation can put several vehicles on the road, and groups of 1,000 to 2,000 guests move on coordinated multi-vehicle service. Scottsdale Sprinters holds the Phoenix Sky Harbor (PHX) ground transportation permit.
